title: Agents and skills
about: Who does a step's work, what it is told, and what it may do.

terms.meaning: who does a step's work: its instructions, its tools, its fence and its skills, written once and named by the steps it works on.
an agent's name: its file's in the agents' folder, without its extension, by which a step names it.
what a person adds to an agent they use, one file per agent in their store, without rewriting it.

what a step's session may do with its tools, in one shape for every harness, each harness's own keys inside its block (`claude: { fence: … }`, `codex: { fence: … }`): on Claude Code its permission mode and its allowed and denied calls (`allowedTools`, `disallowedTools`), on Codex its sandbox. A step's fence only narrows its agent's.

the files the harness itself reads in the folder an agent works in, `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`, which hold for every agent at work there; the third layer, above the agent's own instructions and below the factory's rules.

the five layers of what an agent is told, numbered by precedence: its instructions, a person's custom instructions, the folder's files, the factory's rules, and the step's policy. Where two say different things the higher number wins, and the task is above them all, and a session is told so: each layer Nemia composes is headed by its number and its owner, and every brief opens on the precedence in words.

what an agent lets a step override of it, on its own `overridable:` line, each word one of `OVERRIDABLE`: `fence` for every fence key at once, `skills` and `mcp`, which only add, and the role keys. A step that sets anything else is refused at load, naming the key and the agent; an agent with no line offers everything.
the keys a step's own file sets over its agent's fence and composition (`OVERRIDE_KEYS`): the fence keys, which only narrow the agent's, and `skills` and `mcp`, which only add.

retired.card: decision 12, slice 1: a harness's fence under its block, and what a step may override

terms.meaning: a folder of instructions and files an agent is given for one kind of work: its `SKILL.md`, whose frontmatter gives its card entry — a one-line description, required — and whether it is loaded every turn (`preload:`).
the name of a skill's folder: lowercase words joined by dashes, 64 characters at most.

the agent on a step (AgentOnStep): the agent a step is given, by its `agent:` line or by a factory's hire, and what the step overrides of it (`overridesOf`), which the agent's `overridable:` must offer.
the only tools a step's session has (`tools`), beside its fence.

the one way an agent and a person's custom instructions for it are read and written: `AgentDoor` in `packages/agent-orchestrator/src/agents/agent-door.store.ts`, rooted as the Factory door is, its files layer over today's agent files and a memory one, each write checked by the agent's name, the model's `Agent` and the version it was read at (`definitionVersionRefusal`) before either layer acts.

the one way a skill is found, read, written and copied: `SkillDoor` in `packages/agent-orchestrator/src/skills/skill-door.store.ts`, rooted as the Agent door is, through the same lookup roots and the one precedence (`lookedUp`), each write checked by the skill's name, the model's `Skill` and the version it was read at.
